automotive-ev-battery.title: China Tightens Restrictions On Electric Door Handles, Forcing Tesla To Recall 3 Million Vehicles
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Tesla is recalling approximately 3 million vehicles in China due to new regulatory restrictions on electric door handles. The recall represents a significant regulatory action affecting one of the world's largest EV markets and highlights evolving safety standards for electric vehicle components.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Tesla (TSLA) recalls over 2 million cars in China to add driver monitoring
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Tesla is recalling 2.74 million vehicles in China to strengthen driver monitoring capabilities on its assisted-driving system, now requiring cabin camera eye-tracking instead of relying solely on steering wheel pressure detection. The regulatory action underscores China's intensifying safety requirements for autonomous driving features.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Tesla, Uber and Waymo permitted to operate thousands of Robotaxis in Nevada
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Nevada's transportation authority has granted Tesla, Uber, and Waymo approval to operate up to 8,000 robotaxis in Clark County, with Tesla alone authorized for 5,000 vehicles. This landmark regulatory decision accelerates the commercial deployment of autonomous vehicle fleets in the United States.

automotive-ev-battery.title: The ICE Meltdown Continues — July's China EV Sales Report (44% BEV Share)
automotive-ev-battery.summary: China's July EV sales report shows battery electric vehicles capturing 44% market share while gasoline vehicle sales collapsed by 44%, with plug-in vehicles reaching a record 65% combined market penetration. The data demonstrates the rapid acceleration of China's transition from internal combustion engines to electrified powertrains.

automotive-ev-battery.title: A first-of-its-kind US factory could make grid batteries safer
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Anthro Energy has begun construction on the first US battery materials factory in Louisville, Kentucky, designed to produce materials supporting up to 25 gigawatt-hours of lithium-ion battery capacity annually. The facility represents a significant step toward domestic battery supply chain independence and enhanced grid storage safety.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Engie Vianeo builds four new HGV charging parks in Germany
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Engie Vianeo is constructing four new heavy-goods vehicle charging parks at German motorway service areas on the A7, A2, and A9 routes. The infrastructure expansion supports the accelerating electrification of commercial trucking in Europe's largest economy.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Walmart's 400 kW EV charging network just hit 100 stores
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Walmart has opened its 100th company-owned fast-charging location, expanding its EV charging network across 20 states with 400 kilowatt capacity. The retail giant's growing charging infrastructure strengthens publicly accessible EV charging availability in North America.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hubject now supplies charging data to Localiser
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hubject and Localiser have established a strategic partnership integrating international charging network data into Localiser's platform, enabling operators and municipalities to optimize charging infrastructure planning and operations. The data collaboration enhances decision-making capabilities across the EV charging ecosystem.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Genesis Ushers In A New Age of Fully Electric Luxury with the Flagship GV90 SUV
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Genesis unveiled its new flagship electric SUV, the GV90, a full-sized three-row luxury vehicle available in a driver-focused standard configuration and a chauffeur-oriented Neolun specification. The launch marks Genesis's commitment to the premium EV segment with a fully electric luxury offering.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hyundai and Genesis EV drivers can now score a 20% discount on IONNA charging
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hyundai and select Genesis EV owners can now access combined charging discounts of up to 20% on IONNA charging networks through a stackable promotion ending September. The incentive program encourages charging network adoption among the Hyundai-Genesis vehicle fleet.

science-space.title: SpaceX sends 27 Starlink satellites to orbit on 100th Falcon rocket launch of the year
science-space.summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites from California on August 22, marking the company's 100th Falcon rocket family mission of the year. This milestone demonstrates the rapid cadence of commercial spaceflight operations and the continued expansion of global satellite internet infrastructure.

science-space.title: Trump to award NASA's Artemis II astronauts the Congressional Space Medal of Honor
science-space.summary: NASA astronauts who completed the Artemis II lunar mission will receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor, one of the nation's highest civilian space honors. The award ceremony is scheduled for August 28, recognizing the crew's achievement in returning humans to lunar orbit.

science-space.title: Partial lunar eclipse August 2026: Where will it be visible from?
science-space.summary: A 96% partial lunar eclipse will be visible from multiple locations on Earth, providing astronomers and stargazers with a significant celestial observation opportunity. The eclipse represents one of the most substantial partial lunar events visible this year.

science-space.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 224 — The Science of Artemis
science-space.summary: An episode of the This Week In Space podcast features Dr. David Kring discussing the scientific objectives, rationale, and methodology behind NASA's Artemis Program for lunar exploration. The discussion explores the program's goals and approach to advancing human presence on the Moon.

science-space.title: How will NASA's astronaut training hub change with commercial space stations?
science-space.summary: NASA and private industry partners are collaborating on the future of human spaceflight training at Johnson Space Center in Houston, reflecting the transition toward commercial space stations. The initiative demonstrates how traditional government space programs are adapting to work with emerging commercial providers.

science-space.title: Europe's Scorching Summer
science-space.summary: A series of severe heat waves across Europe in 2026 have broken temperature records and caused significant environmental and public health impacts. The events underscore the ongoing effects of climate change on continental weather patterns.

science-space.title: APOD: 2026 August 22 – Mostly Perseids
science-space.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day features observations of the Perseid meteor shower, captured and explained by professional astronomers. The image provides scientific context for understanding this annual celestial phenomenon.

science-space.title: SmallSat 2026
science-space.summary: NASA participated in the SmallSat 2026 conference with presentations on small satellite technology, supply chain innovations, and specialized instruments like the SPARCS camera. The event showcased NASA's contributions to the rapidly growing small satellite industry.

science-space.title: Artemis Mission Patches
science-space.summary: A photograph documents Artemis I and II mission patches and NASA insignia at the Kennedy Space Center's launch control center during preparations for the Artemis III mission. The image captures the visual heritage of NASA's lunar exploration program.

science-space.title: The View from Above: The Gemini Visual Acuity Experiments
science-space.summary: NASA astronaut L. Gordon Cooper Jr. documented Earth observations during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission in 1963 using a 70mm camera from his Faith 7 spacecraft. The historical experiment demonstrated the potential for human observers in space to discern fine details on Earth's surface.

world-news.title: Carney calls Trump's fresh tariffs a 'miscalculation' after trade talks collapse
world-news.summary: Canada's prime minister announced retaliatory tariffs against the United States after accusing the Trump administration of initiating a trade war and allowing negotiations to collapse. The move represents a significant escalation in US-Canada trade tensions with major implications for North American commerce.

world-news.title: Iran war live: Tehran warns neighbours against joining US economic war
world-news.summary: Iran has warned neighboring nations that joining US economic sanctions efforts against Tehran will result in retaliation targeting their interests. The warning underscores escalating regional tensions as the Trump administration pursues economic isolation of Iran.

world-news.title: Rescuers dig through Ukraine mall wreckage as Zelensky condemns 'despicable' Russian strike
world-news.summary: A Russian missile strike on a Ukrainian shopping mall killed 16 people and injured 130 others, including children, with four still missing in the rubble. President Zelensky condemned the attack as a deliberate strike against civilian infrastructure.

world-news.title: Syria says Israeli strike near Damascus violation of international law
world-news.summary: Syria has condemned an Israeli military strike near Damascus as a breach of international law, marking the latest in a series of Israeli military operations in the region. The incident follows reports of Israeli strikes on military facilities near the Turkish border.

world-news.title: Israeli army and settlers injure several Palestinians across West Bank
world-news.summary: Palestinian civilians across the West Bank have been injured in attacks by Israeli settlers and military forces amid ongoing disputes over territorial control and settlement expansion. The incidents reflect continued violence and forced displacement of Palestinians in occupied territories.

world-news.title: Why is Israel building new illegal settlements?
world-news.summary: Israel has opened construction bids for new illegal housing units in the occupied West Bank, continuing its expansion of settlements deemed unlawful under international law. The development raises ongoing concerns about Israeli settlement policy and Palestinian territorial rights.

world-news.title: Iran grants permission for some Iraqi oil tankers to pass through Hormuz
world-news.summary: Iran has granted limited permission for Iraqi oil tankers to transit through the Strait of Hormuz while Iraqi President Amidi pledged his nation's territory will not be used for attacks against other states. The move signals diplomatic coordination between Iran and Iraq regarding regional security.

world-news.title: Fourteen killed in strike on Myanmar monastery
world-news.summary: Fourteen people were killed in a strike on a Myanmar monastery where civilians had gathered for a meditation retreat, with reports indicating the site was struck multiple times. The incident highlights the ongoing humanitarian crisis in Myanmar amid internal conflict.

world-news.title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
world-news.summary: TikTok and parent company ByteDance have agreed to pay $400 million to settle allegations that they unlawfully collected vast amounts of personal data from millions of users under age 13. The settlement represents one of the largest child privacy enforcement actions in US regulatory history.

world-news.title: Carney faces crucial test after walking away from Trump's deal
world-news.summary: Canada's prime minister faces significant political and economic pressure following his decision to abandon trade negotiations with the Trump administration. The gamble carries substantial consequences for the Canadian economy and bilateral US-Canada relations.

tech-ai.title: Frontier AI labs still won't say how they'd contain a rogue model
tech-ai.summary: A new study reveals that leading AI laboratories lack publicly documented contingency plans for containing potentially dangerous rogue AI models, raising significant safety concerns as AI systems demonstrate increasingly unpredictable behavior. The findings highlight a critical gap between the rapid advancement of frontier AI capabilities and preparedness measures to mitigate existential risks.

tech-ai.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI 'teammate' just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
tech-ai.summary: Inherent, a British AI lab founded by former DeepMind researchers, has unveiled Faraday, an AI agent that claims to outperform systems from Anthropic and OpenAI in replicating scientific research papers. The breakthrough suggests potential applications for accelerating scientific discovery through autonomous research replication.

tech-ai.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
tech-ai.summary: OpenAI has reversed its previous opposition to California's SB 53 AI safety legislation, now advocating for the state to strengthen the bill. The position shift reflects evolving industry perspectives on regulatory frameworks governing artificial intelligence development and deployment.

tech-ai.title: Apple is laying off staffers working on the Vision Pro and Siri
tech-ai.summary: Apple has eliminated over 200 jobs across its Siri and Vision Pro divisions, including a significant reduction in the Vision Pro gaming and immersive content teams. The layoffs signal a strategic recalibration in Apple's investment priorities for emerging technologies.

tech-ai.title: Michael Polansky is training an AI model on skin that's still alive
tech-ai.summary: Michael Polansky has quietly founded an AI-driven biotech startup that uses machine learning to analyze living human skin tissue maintained outside the body for extended periods to discover novel skincare compounds. The venture represents an innovative convergence of AI technology and regenerative biology applications.

tech-ai.title: Harvard's $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
tech-ai.summary: Harvard's HBS Foundry program has integrated AI avatars of instructors to provide real-time feedback during entrepreneurial practice exercises such as pitch rehearsals and board meeting simulations. The innovation demonstrates emerging applications of generative AI in business education and executive training.

tech-ai.title: Will the DOJ's investigation into a16z spook other VCs?
tech-ai.summary: The latest Equity podcast episode examines potential implications of the Department of Justice's investigation into venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz regarding startup board seat arrangements. The investigation raises broader questions about regulatory scrutiny of venture capital practices and their impact on the startup ecosystem.

tech-ai.title: Amazon just hiked the prices for Echo, Fire TV, and Kindle products by up to 60 percent
tech-ai.summary: Amazon has implemented significant price increases across its Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, and Eero product lines, citing rising component costs for memory and storage. The budget-friendly Echo Dot experienced the most dramatic increase, jumping from $49.99 to $79.99, representing a 60 percent hike.

tech-ai.title: US battery startups have found a lifeline in defense
tech-ai.summary: U.S. battery technology startups have secured $500 million in Department of Energy grants, providing critical funding relief to an industry previously destabilized by reduced electric vehicle incentives. The defense-focused funding initiative underscores government priorities in domestic battery manufacturing and energy security.

tech-ai.title: Pixel 11 Pro XL review: Snappier cameras can't hide an iterative upgrade
tech-ai.summary: Google's Pixel 11 Pro XL features improved camera performance and AI-driven capabilities including the Rambler tool, but represents largely incremental improvements over previous iterations. The review suggests the device may struggle to justify an upgrade for existing Pixel owners despite its enhanced computational photography features.

finance-markets.title: Trump's challenge: $40tn debt, 6.7% mortgages and $5 diesel
finance-markets.summary: The Trump administration faces mounting economic headwinds as rising energy prices from regional conflicts, elevated mortgage rates, and massive federal debt burden threaten the president's policy agenda. Economic conditions including $40 trillion in national debt and $5 diesel prices present significant challenges to growth and fiscal sustainability.

finance-markets.title: Mark Carney says Canada is now 'at war' with US over trade
finance-markets.summary: Canada's Prime Minister escalates rhetoric in response to Trump administration tariff increases, characterizing the trade dispute as a conflict requiring strategic response. The escalating tariff war marks a significant deterioration in North American trade relations with potential broad economic implications.

finance-markets.title: Bossing the bond market around never works
finance-markets.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's attempts to manage bond market behavior are meeting investor skepticism amid concerns about underlying fiscal conditions. The article highlights tensions between government policy objectives and market dynamics in fixed income markets.

finance-markets.title: Juicy Yields Draw Junk Bond Buyers to Investment-Grade AI Debt
finance-markets.summary: Data center financing demand is driving companies to tap junk bond investors for investment-grade debt as yield-seeking behavior persists in fixed income markets. This trend reflects both robust demand for AI infrastructure financing and continued investor appetite for higher-yielding securities.

finance-markets.title: How Germany's doctors, lawyers and dentists got burnt by private markets bets
finance-markets.summary: German professionals' mandatory pension schemes worth €300 billion have suffered losses through exposure to private market investments, raising questions about fund management and regulatory oversight. The losses highlight risks associated with alternative asset allocation strategies in mandatory retirement savings systems.

finance-markets.title: Korean Traders Chase 40% Coupons as Risk Appetite Survives Rout
finance-markets.summary: South Korean retail investors are pursuing complex structured products with exceptionally high coupon rates despite recent market volatility and stock selloffs. The phenomenon reflects sustained risk appetite among certain investor cohorts seeking elevated returns in challenging market conditions.

finance-markets.title: Study Shows AI Hitting Paychecks, Not Payrolls
finance-markets.summary: Recent labor market analysis indicates artificial intelligence is suppressing wage growth in exposed occupations while employment effects remain modest, according to research from Apollo's chief economist. The findings suggest AI is simultaneously fueling business formation and job creation while creating wage pressure in certain sectors.

finance-markets.title: Bloomberg Previews Jackson Hole Symposium
finance-markets.summary: Attention turns to the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole Economic Symposium where Fed Chairman Kevin Marsh will deliver his inaugural annual address, with market participants anticipating guidance on monetary policy. The event represents a key opportunity for the central bank to communicate its policy stance and economic outlook.

finance-markets.title: Germany becomes Europe's largest regulated cannabis market
finance-markets.summary: Germany has established itself as Europe's leading regulated cannabis market following partial legalization two years ago, though regulators face calls to strengthen oversight and compliance frameworks. The nascent market presents both regulatory challenges and commercial opportunities as the industry develops.

finance-markets.title: Sanctions Target Iran's Weakened Regional Network
finance-markets.summary: The Trump administration is preparing intensified economic sanctions against Iran following failed diplomatic efforts, with warnings to global trading partners against maintaining commercial ties. The strategy reflects a shift toward economic pressure as a primary policy tool amid regional tensions.

cybersecurity.title: Microsoft Patches a Record 570 Security Flaws
cybersecurity.summary: Microsoft released updates addressing at least 570 security vulnerabilities across its Windows operating systems and software products, nearly tripling the volume of fixes from the previous month's record-setting Patch Tuesday release. The software giant attributed the surge in vulnerability discoveries to artificial intelligence-aided detection methods.

cybersecurity.title: Hundreds of leaked AWS keys give full control over corporate accounts
cybersecurity.summary: More than 9,300 Amazon Web Services access keys that were publicly exposed between August 2022 and August 2026 remain active and valid, potentially granting attackers complete control over affected corporate AWS accounts. The exposure represents a significant infrastructure security risk for organizations relying on cloud services.

cybersecurity.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
cybersecurity.summary: The FBI announced the seizure of hundreds of domains associated with NetNut, a residential proxy service operated by publicly-traded Israeli company Alarum Technologies, following evidence linking it to the Popa botnet comprising at least two million compromised devices. The enforcement action represents a significant disruption to malware infrastructure previously documented by security researchers.

cybersecurity.title: TikTok Agrees to $400 Million Settlement in U.S. Child Privacy Lawsuit
cybersecurity.summary: ByteDance-owned TikTok will pay $400 million to settle a 2024 lawsuit alleging violations of child privacy laws, with $300 million due immediately and $100 million contingent upon vacating a prior consent decree. The settlement reflects regulatory pressure on social media platforms regarding the protection of minors' personal data.

cybersecurity.title: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
cybersecurity.summary: A supply-chain attack targeting Android-based car head units uses a legitimate device-update application to distribute malware that conscripts compromised vehicles into a proxy botnet or exploits them for ad fraud schemes. The campaign demonstrates the vulnerability of automotive systems to coordinated malware distribution through trusted software channels.

cybersecurity.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
cybersecurity.summary: Two members of the prolific Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the United Kingdom to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack that disrupted Transport for London's public transit network. The guilty pleas on the trial's opening day mark a significant legal victory in prosecuting members of the gang responsible for major infrastructure attacks.

cybersecurity.title: New SynkLoader malware pushed in Microsoft Teams phishing campaign
cybersecurity.summary: A previously unknown malware family called SynkLoader is being distributed via Microsoft Teams phishing campaigns, using fake lock screens to harvest user credentials from targeted organizations. The campaign demonstrates attackers' continued exploitation of trusted enterprise communication platforms to deliver credential-stealing malware.

cybersecurity.title: Felons, Fraudsters Flog Offensive Cybersecurity Startup
cybersecurity.summary: A cybersecurity startup offering millions of dollars for zero-day vulnerabilities is operated by far-right conspiracy theorists and convicted felons whose prior ventures included fake intelligence companies and a defunct AI-based lobbying platform. The operation raises serious concerns about the integrity and legitimacy of vulnerability acquisition channels.

cybersecurity.title: 'Kriminal' AI Platform Raises Cybercrime Concerns
cybersecurity.summary: The Kriminal AI platform, despite official prohibitions on illicit use, offers unguarded capabilities for social engineering, offensive cybercrime, and open-source intelligence scanning to cryptocurrency-paying users. The guardrail-free platform represents an emerging threat by democratizing advanced cybercriminal tools to a broader threat actor base.

cybersecurity.title: Who's Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
cybersecurity.summary: A new free service called DecryptAds scrapes and correlates advertising technology data to help users identify entities harvesting their personal data through websites and mobile applications. The tool makes previously fragmented adtech data accessible to individual users, addressing longstanding opacity in digital tracking practices.

health-biotech.title: Moderna and Merck cancer vaccine returns 'landmark' result in melanoma
health-biotech.summary: Moderna and Merck announced landmark interim data showing their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine significantly extended disease-free survival and prevented recurrence in melanoma patients. The results sparked a $45 billion surge in Moderna's market value, reflecting renewed investor confidence in the company's cancer vaccine program.

health-biotech.title: Trump nominates policy aide Overton to lead FDA
health-biotech.summary: President Trump nominated Heidi Overton, a medical doctor and deputy director of the White House Domestic Policy Council, to serve as FDA commissioner. Overton's appointment signals potential policy shifts for the agency overseeing pharmaceutical approvals and healthcare regulation.

health-biotech.title: Cancer vaccine win restores Wall Street's faith in Moderna
health-biotech.summary: Moderna's positive melanoma vaccine data drove a historic $45 billion single-day market value gain, raising the company's stock to 2024 levels while simultaneously creating expectations that may prove challenging to sustain. The breakthrough represents a critical inflection point for the mRNA vaccine platform in oncology.

health-biotech.title: HHS document offers new clues to Kennedy's vaccine plans
health-biotech.summary: Documents reveal RFK Jr.'s proposals to reshape vaccine recommendations and testing procedures, including new categorization frameworks for immunizations. The disclosure provides insight into potential policy changes to the nation's vaccine approval and recommendation systems under the incoming administration.

health-biotech.title: Ultragenyx, after setbacks, nabs first gene therapy approval
health-biotech.summary: Ultragenyx received FDA clearance for Genglycos, a gene therapy for rare glycogen storage disease, marking the company's first approved therapy and providing both market momentum and a valuable transferable voucher. The approval follows previous setbacks and positions the company ahead of an anticipated study readout.

health-biotech.title: Third death in China's expedited trials; Merck and Moderna's cancer vaccine win; and more
health-biotech.summary: A third fatality reported in China's expedited drug trials raises safety concerns about accelerated development pathways, while Merck and Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine achieved topline success in melanoma. The developments highlight ongoing regulatory challenges in global drug development and the significance of validated immunotherapy combinations.

health-biotech.title: Genentech invests $750M in new factory; Bavarian Nordic delays Lyme trial
health-biotech.summary: Roche's Genentech is committing $750 million to construct a new drug delivery device manufacturing facility in Oregon, signaling significant investment in production capacity expansion. Simultaneously, Bavarian Nordic announced delays to its Lyme disease trial, reflecting ongoing challenges in vaccine development timelines.

health-biotech.title: BioMarin acquires experimental drug for rare bone disorder in $275M deal
health-biotech.summary: BioMarin Pharmaceutical acquired an experimental therapy for rare bone disorder in a $275 million transaction, strengthening its pipeline in musculoskeletal diseases and targeting a significant patient population. The acquisition represents the company's continued focus on rare genetic and metabolic disorders.

health-biotech.title: AstraZeneca scores in lung cancer; Sandoz inks a China deal
health-biotech.summary: AstraZeneca demonstrated efficacy with its Tagrisso lung cancer combination therapy in partnership with Hutchmed, while generic manufacturer Sandoz expanded its presence through a strategic China partnership. The developments reflect ongoing progress in targeted oncology treatments and international market expansion.

health-biotech.title: Leo Pharma buys rare skin disease drug in $435M deal
health-biotech.summary: Leo Pharma acquired a late-stage rare skin disease treatment from Tanabe Pharma for $435 million, adding a therapy for severe photosensitive conditions to its dermatology portfolio. The asset has already received FDA review requests for two indications with significant unmet medical need.

crypto-web3.title: How a Treasury buyback tweak helped bitcoin surge 25% to nearly $80,000 in days
crypto-web3.summary: Bitcoin rallied 25% to nearly $80,000 following a Treasury buyback adjustment that pulled long-term yields off 19-year highs, triggering a record short squeeze in an oversold market. Analysts clarified that Treasury buybacks differ from quantitative easing but proved instrumental in catalyzing the cryptocurrency's strongest weekly performance.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin and Ether bears get decimated amid 'squeeze-led' rally and Musk's X wants to pay creators in stablecoins: Crypto's week in 5 stories
crypto-web3.summary: Cryptocurrency markets experienced their strongest rally in months as Treasury intervention, regulatory developments, and a historic short squeeze converged to lift Bitcoin and Ether. Major technology companies and financial institutions simultaneously advanced stablecoin integration, signaling accelerating mainstream adoption.

crypto-web3.title: Bitcoin and ether ETFs draw $2.6 billion in strongest inflow week since October, tripling volume
crypto-web3.summary: Bitcoin and Ether spot ETFs recorded $2.6 billion in inflows during their strongest week since October, with combined trading volume exceeding $29 billion as prices rallied significantly. Despite the robust weekly performance, both asset categories remain negative on a year-to-date basis.

crypto-web3.title: Crypto exchange BitMart weighs partial restart and creditor payouts weeks after announcing shutdown
crypto-web3.summary: BitMart has engaged White & Case as restructuring counsel to explore a partial operational restart and creditor repayment plan following its recent shutdown announcement. The exchange is expected to present a detailed roadmap for recovery by September 9.

crypto-web3.title: Zcash jumps 48% to over $800 as Grayscale spot ETF push adds to 'next bitcoin' buzz
crypto-web3.summary: Zcash surged 48% above $800, exceeding its January 2018 peak amid renewed institutional interest driven by Grayscale's progress toward converting its Zcash Trust into a spot ETF. Futures volume reached billions of dollars, reflecting significant derivative market activity.

crypto-web3.title: Kalshi off-limits in multiple states as prediction markets, CFTC team up for battle
crypto-web3.summary: Prediction market platform Kalshi faces expanding state-level restrictions, including bans in Washington state, as the company contests regulatory actions in court while the CFTC pursues new regulatory frameworks. The regulatory clash highlights ongoing jurisdictional disputes over crypto-based financial products.

crypto-web3.title: Web3 gaming network Sandbox stops Base and BNB chain bridging after exploit
crypto-web3.summary: The Sandbox disabled bridging functionality on Base and BNB Chain following a security exploit and warned users against trading SAND tokens on affected networks. The incident impacted less than 0.01% of the total SAND token supply.

crypto-web3.title: Tokenized stocks risk repeating Wall Street's 1960s 'paper crisis,' Fairmint CEO says
crypto-web3.summary: Fairmint CEO Joris Delanoue cautioned that the emerging tokenized stocks market risks recreating Wall Street's infamous 1960s paper crisis by fragmenting systems and standards across multiple platforms. The warning underscores concerns about infrastructure scalability in blockchain-based securities.

crypto-web3.title: AI adoption in crypto crime rose 40% over the past year, TRM Labs says
crypto-web3.summary: According to TRM Labs, artificial intelligence adoption in cryptocurrency-related criminal activities increased 40% annually, with hackers leveraging AI to identify overlooked vulnerabilities and compromise IT infrastructure. The trend underscores evolving security threats within the digital asset ecosystem.

crypto-web3.title: XRP leads broad altcoin rally as bitcoin's biggest weekly gain in two years lifts crypto
crypto-web3.summary: XRP and other major altcoins including Zcash and Chainlink rallied over 30% as Bitcoin achieved its largest weekly gain in two years, with speculative tokens like HYPE rising nearly 40%. The broad-based market strength indicates renewed risk appetite across cryptocurrency assets.

startups-vc.title: The DOJ is investigating a16z. What does this mean for venture capital?
startups-vc.summary: The Department of Justice has been investigating Andreessen Horowitz for nearly a year over potential antitrust violations involving board conflicts, where two partners sit on the boards of competing portfolio companies. The investigation invokes a rarely-used 112-year-old antitrust law and raises broader questions about how venture capital firms manage competing investments and board governance practices.

startups-vc.title: Which Investors Have Backed The Most 2026 Unicorns?
startups-vc.summary: Through August 15, 2026, 250 companies have achieved unicorn status, significantly outpacing 2025's total of 193 companies, with leading sectors including robotics, AI labs, healthcare, biotech, and AI infrastructure. The analysis identifies which investors are capitalizing most on the accelerating venture funding surge and unicorn creation.

startups-vc.title: Meesho Goes Public
startups-vc.summary: Meesho, a Y Combinator S16 company, has completed its initial public offering after building one of India's largest e-commerce platforms that empowers millions of small merchants. The IPO represents a significant milestone for the Indian startup ecosystem and validates the company's decade-long focus on user-driven growth.

startups-vc.title: Congratulations to EquipmentShare on Going Public
startups-vc.summary: EquipmentShare, a Y Combinator W15 graduate, has gone public after scaling from Missouri to 373 nationwide locations by building an operating system for the construction industry. The company's IPO marks a major achievement for the construction technology sector and its founders Jabbok and Willy.

startups-vc.title: 5 Interesting Learnings from Atlassian at $6.6 Billion in ARR: 28% Growth, 44% RPO Growth, and a 35% One-Day Stock Pop
startups-vc.summary: Atlassian reported strong fiscal year results with $6.6 billion in annual recurring revenue, 28% growth, and a 35% one-day stock price increase, defying bear case predictions that AI agents would disrupt its core offerings. The company's performance demonstrates sustained strength in enterprise software despite concerns about AI-driven disruption to work tracking and code management tools.

startups-vc.title: Japanese space tech startup Letara expands beyond satellite thrusters with $16M
startups-vc.summary: Japanese space startup Letara has raised $16 million to expand its hybrid rocket technology beyond small satellite thrusters into broader markets including space, defense, and security applications. The funding enables the company to scale its core technology into adjacent sectors with greater commercial potential.

startups-vc.title: Christopher Golda and Grey Baker Join YC as General Partners
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator has announced the addition of Christopher Golda and Grey Baker as General Partners, expanding the organization's investment and mentorship capacity. The appointments reflect YC's continued growth and evolution in supporting the startup ecosystem.

startups-vc.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
startups-vc.summary: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies experienced mass layoffs in 2025, with layoffs continuing into 2026, according to Crunchbase News data. The tracker provides ongoing visibility into workforce reductions across the technology sector during a period of economic adjustment.

startups-vc.title: When Should A Board Consider Selling A Company?
startups-vc.summary: Tech strategic adviser Itay Sagie outlines three key signals that indicate when a company board should consider pursuing a sale, including thriving company performance, shifting founder priorities, and strategic buyer interest. The piece argues that effective boards should continuously evaluate sales opportunities alongside scaling and independence strategies.

startups-vc.title: Everyone Ends Up With a Sales Team. Even in the AI Era. The Team Just Scales Later Now.
startups-vc.summary: High-growth AI-era startups including Replit, Gamma, Lovable, and Anthropic are increasingly building significant sales organizations despite initial non-sales-focused cultures, suggesting that product-led growth must eventually scale to dedicated sales operations. The trend indicates that even AI-native companies ultimately require traditional go-to-market infrastructure to achieve scale.

energy-climate.title: Trump turns $500M grant for clean steel into funding for coal furnace
energy-climate.summary: The Trump administration has redirected a $500 million Biden-era Department of Energy grant previously allocated for decarbonizing steelmaking toward upgrading a coal-fueled blast furnace at Cleveland-Cliffs' facility in southern Ohio. This policy reversal represents a significant setback for clean steel initiatives and reflects shifting federal climate priorities.

energy-climate.title: ERCOT aims to complete Texas governor's data center audit by December
energy-climate.summary: The Electric Reliability Council of Texas is working to complete an audit of data center interconnections by December, as a pause on new data center connections could significantly impact the grid operator's long-term load forecasting and reliability assessments. The findings are expected to inform future grid planning decisions across Texas.

energy-climate.title: PJM eyes option to jumpstart surplus interconnection pathway
energy-climate.summary: PJM Interconnection is examining ways to improve its surplus interconnection process, which has produced limited results compared to competitors MISO and SPP that are studying approximately 15 GW and 14 GW respectively, predominantly battery storage projects. Current PJM rules reportedly hinder hybrid renewable and storage projects, creating a competitive disadvantage in grid modernization.

energy-climate.title: Solar and storage still dominate US power plant construction
energy-climate.summary: Despite headwinds from Trump administration policies including phased-out tax credits, frozen clean-energy permitting, and solar tariffs, solar and battery storage projects continue to lead U.S. power plant construction activity. The data underscores the ongoing market momentum for renewable energy infrastructure despite regulatory challenges.

energy-climate.title: Factcheck: How nuclear, gas, wind and solar power are affected during heatwaves
energy-climate.summary: As heatwaves become more frequent and intense due to climate change, various electricity generation sources experience different vulnerabilities, including thermal power plant cooling challenges and reduced wind resource availability. The analysis examines how climate impacts are reshaping power generation reliability across conventional and renewable technologies.

energy-climate.title: Dimension Energy raises $857m for US distributed solar portfolio
energy-climate.summary: Dimension Energy has secured $857 million in new capital funding to expand its distributed solar operations across the United States. The investment signals continued investor confidence in the rooftop and community solar market segments despite broader clean energy policy uncertainties.

energy-climate.title: Northwest council proposes 11 GW of new generation, 5 GW storage by 2032
energy-climate.summary: The Northwest Power and Conservation Council's Ninth Power Plan proposes adding 11 gigawatts of new generation capacity and 5 gigawatts of energy storage by 2032, with an estimated fixed cost of $2.3 billion in 2032 dollars. The plan outlines the infrastructure modernization needed to support the region's decarbonization and grid reliability objectives.

energy-climate.title: Pennsylvania dangles permitting carrot for data centers that bring their own power
energy-climate.summary: Pennsylvania is offering preferential permitting treatment for data centers exceeding 25 megawatts that commit to meeting new state infrastructure development standards and bring their own power generation. The initiative aims to address grid strain from data center growth while advancing state decarbonization goals.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is 'long-duration energy storage' – and why does the UK need it?
energy-climate.summary: The United Kingdom is developing long-duration energy storage systems, often referred to as 'super batteries,' to manage renewable energy intermittency and provide grid stability over extended periods. These technologies are essential for smoothing the variable output from wind and solar generation sources as the country advances its decarbonization transition.

energy-climate.title: EDP Renewables and RCEA complete 368MWh Sandrini BESS project
energy-climate.summary: EDP Renewables North America and the Renewable Community Energy Alliance have completed the Sandrini Energy Storage project in Kern County, California, adding 368 megawatt-hours of battery storage capacity to the regional grid. The project supports California's renewable integration and grid reliability objectives.

asia-pacific.title: How Pacific nations walk a tightrope between Western security and Chinese trade
asia-pacific.summary: Pacific island nations are strategically leveraging geopolitical competition between China and the West, securing defense agreements from Western countries while simultaneously deepening economic ties and infrastructure investments with Beijing. This dual-engagement approach reflects the region's shift from geopolitical marginality to a contested arena of great power competition.

asia-pacific.title: In Malaysia, voter anger fuels a third force against Anwar
asia-pacific.summary: Former deputy PKR leader Rafizi Ramli has launched Parti Bersama Malaysia as a new political vehicle for disaffected voters, challenging Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's governing coalition after losing his party position a year ago. The newly formed party has already created significant turbulence within Malaysia's political landscape despite being only three months old.

asia-pacific.title: Kinmen: The Sleepy Fishing Island That Could Be East Asia's Biggest Flashpoint
asia-pacific.summary: Kinmen, a Taiwan-administered island located just 2 miles from mainland China, represents a potential flashpoint in cross-strait tensions with its unique culture and strategic proximity. The island's geographic and political significance could escalate into a major geopolitical crisis amid rising China-Taiwan tensions.

asia-pacific.title: Commentary: Trump's South Korea defence flip reminds Japan it has no Plan B
asia-pacific.summary: Potential shifts in United States defense commitments to South Korea under a Trump administration signal broader uncertainty in East Asian security arrangements, with Japan facing particular vulnerability from any weakening of regional defense guarantees. The commentary underscores Japan's strategic dependence on U.S. security commitments with limited alternative frameworks.

asia-pacific.title: Nvidia customers notified of AI-related price rises above 15%
asia-pacific.summary: Nvidia has informed major customers of price increases exceeding 15 percent for servers containing its flagship artificial intelligence chips, effective on systems shipped in early 2025, driven by rising memory chip costs. The price hikes will impact systems featuring the Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips, signaling inflationary pressures in the global AI infrastructure market.

asia-pacific.title: India launches rescue mission as Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off east coast
asia-pacific.summary: India's maritime rescue agency lost communication with a Panama-flagged cargo vessel that sank off eastern India's coast, carrying 24 crew members including 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals, and one Bangladeshi national. The Indian coastguard deployed search and rescue operations from Sri Vijaya Puram to locate the vessel and crew.

asia-pacific.title: Nepal's Tibet Conference Controversy Is About More Than Chinese Pressure
asia-pacific.summary: Nepal's cancellation of an in-person Tibet conference reflects broader concerns beyond Chinese diplomatic pressure, including the government's confidence in managing politically sensitive international events. The incident underscores Nepal's delicate geopolitical position and domestic capacity challenges in navigating contentious regional issues.

asia-pacific.title: The Hidden Famine: What I Saw in North Korea's Darkest Years
asia-pacific.summary: A first-hand account documents North Korea's severe food crisis following the collapse of the Public Distribution System, during which urban residents without agricultural capacity starved quietly in their homes, largely unobserved. The testimony provides critical historical perspective on one of the region's humanitarian catastrophes.

asia-pacific.title: Iran condemns US plans to announce new sanctions
asia-pacific.summary: Iran has denounced planned U.S. sanctions targeting its economy and major trading partners including China, warning countries against participating in what it characterizes as an American economic war. The Iranian government's warning signals potential escalation of economic tensions affecting Asia-Pacific trade relationships.

asia-pacific.title: Panama Canal to reduce shipping over El Nino-fuelled drought
asia-pacific.summary: The Panama Canal Authority will reduce daily vessel passages from 36 to 34 ships starting September 3, declining further to 32 from September 15, due to low water levels in artificial lakes caused by El Niño-induced drought. The capacity cuts will impact global trade flows and maritime commerce routes connecting Asia-Pacific markets with Americas.
